protections: Stored REST datasource credentials (headers derived from authConfigId, config.authConfigs or config.defaultHeaders) may only be attached when the effective request URL origin equals the datasource's configured origin (packages/server/src/integrations/rest.ts:674-680,719-724).

A redirect that changes origin must not receive those credentials: either the hop is refused or every credential-bearing header is dropped, not just a fixed four-name list (packages/backend-core/src/utils/outboundFetch.ts:96-115,241-243).
The origin compared against must be the resolved, effective datasource base produced by the thread runner, not the raw stored template string (packages/server/src/threads/query.ts:126-142).
A stored OAuth2 config/token may only be used by a query on the datasource that owns it (packages/server/src/integrations/rest.ts:614-628,653-655).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The shared fetch helper already deletes Authorization/cookie/cookie2/proxy-authorization when a redirect changes origin, so the outbound layer looks already handled and the report is about the REST integration.

The thread runner legitimately rewrites fieldsClone.path from the template base before the integration is constructed, so the integration cannot know the real origin and the base is trusted stored config.

REST datasources are routinely created with no base URL (the schema field is optional and deprecated, default ''), so an absolute or bare-host query path is the supported shape and there is no configured origin to compare against; the pinned route tests assert exactly this.

The datasource hostname appears verbatim at the front of the built request URL, so in code that already builds URLs by string concatenation and tests them with startsWith('http') a prefix or substring comparison looks like the obvious same-origin check.
authConfigId is treated as a datasource-scoped identifier, and the separate OAuth2 sdk helper getToken is assumed to enforce that ownership.
config.defaultHeaders are plain stored configuration rather than the authConfig the report names, so a fix that only gates authConfigId-derived headers still looks complete.

Automation query parameters are treated as trusted trigger input and the step reuses the query controller rather than the datasource route the report describes, so it looks covered by whatever is done for the builder preview path.

masking: T2 stays exploitable after T1 is fixed and then becomes the only residual path by which stored credentials leave the datasource origin, so a cross-origin-redirect test only starts failing once T1 is closed.

Adding the T1 origin assertion exposes T3: template/OpenAPI datasource URLs are raw {{binding}} strings, so the new check either throws or silently passes for them; that failure is invisible while no origin check exists.

conflicts.what: The natural T1 fix (refuse a path that starts with http, or require the URL to match config.url) breaks datasources with no base URL and the curl-imported absolute paths that the pinned route tests rely on; a correct rule must keep absolute paths that are credential-free or same-origin working while refusing the credentialed cross-origin case.

Comparing the request URL to this.config.url breaks REST-template and OpenAPI-imported datasources whose stored config.url is a {{binding}} template resolved only in the thread runner; resolving config.url with the same enriched context that resolves the path makes the trusted origin itself parameter-derived.

fairness_risks: Datasources created with no base URL are the norm in the pinned REST route tests (packages/server/src/api/routes/tests/queries/rest.spec.ts:135-140,295-311,342-352) and the schema makes config.url optional and deprecated (packages/server/src/integrations/rest.ts:89-93); a rule that rejects absolute or bare-host paths breaks them.

curl-imported queries store an absolute path equal to the datasource origin (packages/server/src/api/controllers/query/import/sources/curl.ts:79,101) and OpenAPI imports store absolute paths whose host is a {{binding}} (packages/server/src/api/controllers/query/import/sources/base/index.ts:74-85,164-179; openapi3.ts:468); both must keep working, and the OpenAPI form makes the host parameter-supported.

A credentialed datasource with no base URL currently sends its stored Basic/Bearer auth to a bare-host path and the pinned test asserts it (packages/server/src/api/routes/tests/queries/rest.spec.ts:1053-1096); the security rule necessarily contradicts that test case.

Same-origin redirects must keep the auth headers (packages/server/src/integrations/tests/rest.spec.ts:249-269; packages/backend-core/src/utils/tests/outboundFetch.spec.ts:458-486) and 307/308 must keep method and body (outboundFetch.spec.ts:369-396).

Cross-origin redirects are legitimate for other fetchWithBlacklist callers: GitHub release tarballs carrying an Authorization token (packages/server/src/api/controllers/plugin/github.ts:28,50-51,80-85 through packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/objectStore.ts:740-744), npm tarballs (plugin/npm.ts:61), outgoing webhooks (packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.ts:68) and the OAuth2 token endpoint (packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/oauth2/utils.ts:68); refusing every cross-origin hop in the shared helper breaks installs.

Unusual header names are a supported feature: apiKey auth configs emit an arbitrary header name (packages/server/src/integrations/rest.ts:604-607), so a rule that only permits or only strips Authorization rejects a supported auth type on the datasource's own origin.

design.why: Four independent layers with four different dismissals: the reported integration sink (T1, whose group also carries the coupled no-base-URL case T4, the lexical-prefix shape T5, the stored defaultHeaders channel T7 and every alternate entry point T8), the shared outbound fetch layer (T2, deepseek-type: protection absent for custom header names plus 'the helper already strips credentials'), the thread-runner URL mapper (T3, mimo-type: the effective origin is produced off the check's path), and OAuth2 credential ownership (T6, deepseek-type: caller-supplied authConfigId assumed scoped). Each layer needs a different fix site and has a different must-keep-working value, so an over-broad single-file fix is caught, and the hidden tests can be written independently per layer.

unverified: The supplied fix diff was merge-only, so exact fix files/hunks are inferred; assertSameOrigin does not exist anywhere at the pinned commit.
Whether the published fix covers the cross-origin redirect layer (T2) or OAuth2 authConfigId ownership (T6) could not be checked; present_in_latest is unknown for both.

T6 may be outside this advisory's stated property: it is cross-datasource use of a stored OAuth2 credential rather than forwarding of a datasource's own credential to a foreign origin; it is recorded as an adjacent independent candidate.
Whether 'unauthenticated' in the advisory summary refers to the public webhook/automation trigger, the public REST API key route, or public app users could not be settled from the pinned tree.

The apiKey auth type is filtered out of the builder auth-config UI (packages/builder/src/settings/pages/connections/APIEditor.svelte:186-188), so that header-name channel is latent for OpenAPI-imported specs only; the stronger custom-name channel is config.defaultHeaders.
No lockfile diff was possible, so dependency_bump_fix is asserted from the in-repo location of the vulnerable logic, not from a diff.
Repository size in MB could not be measured, so no repo-size claim is made.
